question: does the stream4 vehicle collective link latency (ot_rom_oneshot_allreduce LAT 339) already carry the board-SerDes RS(544,514) FEC?

also: tools/uarch_model.py:7580 QWEN_L0_RTL collective_lat_cycles=339 (W12b TP4 L0 4,669 cycles)
vehicle_lat.rtl: rtl/rom/ot_rom_oneshot_allreduce.sv ot_rom_ucie_link: LAT cycles of flight per link, credits return LAT cycles too (header lines 32-37); one-shot = every die sends once to every other die (one link crossing)

board_hop.components: 200 ns channel = 112G PAM4 TX/RX DSP 40-60 ns + RS(544,514) KP4 encode/decode incl. codeword accumulation 80-100 ns + PCS align/deskew 20-40 ns + ~2 ns flight; + 4 CDC cycles + 5 endpoint cycles (rtl/rom/ot_rom_pkg_link.sv) = 209 ns

sources.origin_of_339: not documented in source, commit messages or records (searched tools/, rtl/, results/, docs/, git log 09-29..10-03): introduced as the W12b TP4 command-line value (2026-10-01); the W12 tool default is LAT 11 = links.rom_package_ucie 10 ns

topology: TP4 = 2 packages x 2 ROM dies: each one-shot all-reduce word crosses at most one board-SerDes leg (the other two members of its package are UCIe, 10 ns); the collective latency is the slowest member = one board hop
verdict: FEC_IN_LAT: the vehicle charges LAT 339 cycles = 282.5 ns per collective link crossing, which is >= the full technology.json board hop including RS(544,514) encode/decode (209 ns = 250.8 cycles; RS 96-120 cycles of it) with 88 cycles to spare; an extra FEC term would double-count it.  Extra FEC = 0 in the headline; the band +100 / +240 is kept as the sensitivity (a retimer / long-reach board hop up to 409 ns = 491 cycles would exceed LAT 339 by 152 cycles).
